title: Insurance Claim Services Notice of the Insured's Right to Withdraw an Arrangement
content:
**Notice.** The claim file must be in opened status when the arrangement is withdrawn. Withdrawal is the insured's own act. The insured may withdraw the arrangement only no later than the withdrawal window after the arrangement instrument was signed. The withdrawal window is counted in calendar days starting the day after the claim file's assignment signed date, and a withdrawal on the last day of the window is in time. On tiers that do not allow withdrawal after work, no water, fire, mold or contents job linked to the claim file may have been authorized and no rebuild contract linked to it may have been signed. After withdrawal the carrier pays the insured directly, and every job of the loss is billed to the customer as self-pay. A withdrawal request outside these conditions is handed to a human representative as not covered by policy.

This notice covers withdrawal of any Insurance Claim Services arrangement — the direction to pay, the assignment or the claim support arrangement. The window and whether withdrawal after work is allowed are each tier's own figures.

## Conditions, all on the system records

| Condition | Evidence |
|---|---|
| claim file in opened status | the claim file's status |
| within the window | the instrument signing date (assignment signed date) on the claim file |
| on tiers not allowing withdrawal after work: no linked water, fire, mold or contents job authorized and no linked rebuild contract signed | the authorization dates of the linked jobs and the signing date of the linked rebuild contract |

## The window, both sides (hypothetical: a 7-day window, instrument signed 10 June)

| Withdrawal on | In time? |
|---|---|
| 11 June (day 1) | yes |
| 17 June (day 7, the last day) | yes |
| 18 June | no; handed to a human representative as not covered by policy |

## Effect

After withdrawal the carrier pays the insured directly and every job of the loss is billed to the customer as self-pay.
